summary: A conditional shortcut survives delivery: when the quotient denominator is x^4, choosing the answer with the largest visible exponent succeeds on all 288 permitted parameter combinations.

source_analysis.skill: Simplify a two-term integrand, apply the sum and constant factor rules, and integrate each power.
reasoning_steps: Expand the product or divide the numerator termwise.
Extract coefficients and integrate each power.
Combine the primitives with one arbitrary constant.
invariants: Preserve two elementary power integrals and moderate workload.
Radio questions require one uniquely correct primitive.
Blanks preceding +C exclude the supplied constant.
permitted_variations: Vary coefficients, signs, eligible exponents and correct-choice positions.
Vary distractor ranks within recognizable quotient profiles.

decision_variation.details: The shortcut succeeds on 288/288 permitted assignments, 17/17 delivered review cases and 2/2 matching runner items. It persists through the conditional same-band selection reproduction.

findings.description: Denominator x^4 identifies bank candidate 4, which always contains the largest visible exponent. Learners can select by this rank while ignoring the numerator and integration. This cross-term correlation is not an integration rule.

findings.reproduction: Run shortcut_challenge.py with the supplied Python, then the native check-engine on grader-all-input.json. All 288 allowed quotient target=4 combinations accept the largest-exponent selection. Runner question 958fc0b4-3e14-556c-9144-516cb46f6406 exhibits the same cue.
findings.requested_change: Vary primitive and distractor roles within the x^4-denominator profile so exponent rank cannot identify correctness. Preserve source replay and workload, then rerun conditional shortcut probes after delivery filtering. Choice shuffling alone will not fix this.
